title: Chapter 40: New Nightmare Mission
html:
His username had turned purple. According to his profile, the thirty-minute video he had uploaded had now been shared, viewed, recommended, and discussed thousands of times. Most of the attention looked like curiosity rather than expertise.

Still, maybe someone useful is buried in all that noise.He wrote a new thread describing the mirror phenomenon and used his account privileges to mark it as a bounty question.

“After the events in my previous video, I’ve encountered repeated unexplained activity involving mirrors. Looking for serious information on how to stop or contain it.”

Replies appeared almost immediately.

“OP, you’re still alive?”

“My grandmother would tell you to hang a lucky charm and stop looking into mirrors after midnight.”

“Call a professional instead of asking strangers on a ghost forum.”

“Maybe it isn’t something to destroy. If ghosts are memories, perhaps you need to understand what keeps it here.”

“Have you tried talking to it? Education solves everything!”

“If there’s something strange in your neighborhood…”

“Then maybe don’t take advice from anonymous internet commenters.”

“My cousin swears you need exactly thirteen beans, three coins, and a red umbrella. Source: my cousin.”

One user posted an obviously fabricated horror story that became so ridiculous halfway through that Chen Ge skipped the rest.

Another insisted that an antique ritual object would solve everything, without offering a single credible reason why.

Chen Ge scrolled for several minutes. Nothing looked reliable. The thread was a mixture of folklore, jokes, and confident nonsense.

He set his phone aside. Whatever he did next, he was not going to gamble his safety on anonymous forum advice.

After going in circles, Chen Ge returned to the black phone. It remained the only source that had consistently corresponded with the supernatural events around him, although its rewards always came with requirements of their own.

Several days of experimentation had revealed a rough pattern. Easy and Normal Missions tended to reward items or upgrades for the Haunted House, while Nightmare Missions offered abilities or objects that affected Chen Ge more directly.

If he wanted something that might help him personally deal with the mirror problem, a Nightmare Mission seemed the most likely path. That did not make the prospect appealing. Nightmare Missions were consistently the least predictable.

Do I take the risk now, or wait until I know more?

Only then did he notice that midnight had passed and the Daily Missions had refreshed.

Easy Mission: A frightening experience still needs rhythm. If every scare comes too early, visitors quickly become numb to it. Install basic monitoring equipment so you can understand how guests move through the attraction and pace the experience accordingly.

Normal Mission: You have met the requirements for the Haunted House’s first expansion. Find a suitable location. Until additional space is secured, no new Trial Missions can be accepted.

Nightmare Mission: Strange sounds can be heard from the bathroom every midnight. If you want to learn their source, follow the instructions.

Daily Missions refresh at midnight. The user may accept only one each day, and rewards correspond to mission difficulty.

Warning: More difficult missions carry greater risk. Choose carefully.

The Normal Mission was impossible until he secured more space, leaving only the Easy and Nightmare options.

Once Uncle Xu brings the money tomorrow, I can start buying monitoring equipment, but installing everything will take time. The Nightmare Mission is connected to the bathroom, though… and that feels uncomfortably relevant.

Neither option was ideal. The Easy Mission might take longer than a day, while the Nightmare Mission could introduce an entirely new problem before he had solved the first.

He sat in the props room weighing the choice. Before he could decide, the scraping sound began again—louder this time. Chen Ge looked toward the ceiling. It was coming from the third floor once more.

I already carried all four dolls downstairs. What else is it tearing at?The creature was becoming more troublesome by the minute. Chen Ge tucked the repaired dolls into his pocket and hurried back to the third floor. When he reached the entrance to Murder by Midnight, what he found there stopped him short.

Fragments of mirror littered the floor outside the entrance, and fresh scratches scored the wooden door.

It has been clawing at the door. What is it trying to do?

Cold sweat prickled across Chen Ge’s back. The thought of that thing roaming the building while he slept was enough to erase any hesitation. Whatever it was, he could not let it continue moving freely through the Haunted House.

Usually easygoing, Chen Ge wore a grim expression as he locked the scenario door behind him and searched the third floor room by room. Wherever he found an intact mirror, he destroyed it. The crash of breaking glass echoed through the empty building until, at last, the corridor fell quiet again.

During the first Nightmare Mission, the doll in front of the mirror managed to hold it back. When it targeted He San, Xiao Wan’s arrival forced it to retreat. But after what happened to He Feng, it can apparently leave the mirror—and it is getting stronger fast.

He could not afford to wait. The Haunted House was finally recovering; he refused to let an unknown presence ruin everything he had rebuilt.

After securing the scenario once more, Chen Ge took out the black phone and accepted the Nightmare Mission with a resolve that surprised even him.I just hope the reward is useful enough to justify this.

“Are you sure you wish to accept the Nightmare Mission? Once accepted, unforeseen circumstances may occur.”

“Yes.”

The screen brightened, and the full mission description appeared.
